GROUP_PTEROSAUR: Pterosaur: a flying reptile, not a dinosaur
GROUP_MOSASAUR: Mosasaur: a sea lizard, not a dinosaur
INFO_TREX_HABITAT: Forested river plains and coastal swamps of western North America.
INFO_TREX_TRAITS: The strongest bite of any land animal, able to crush bone. A huge sense of smell, forward-facing eyes and tiny two-fingered arms.
INFO_TREX_SPECULATIVE: Mostly scaly skin, with fluffy feathers possible on the young. It may have rumbled with its mouth closed like a crocodile instead of roaring, and both hunted and scavenged.
INFO_TREX_FUN_FACT: T. rex lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
INFO_TRIKE_HABITAT: Warm floodplains full of ferns, cycads and palms in western North America.
INFO_TRIKE_TRAITS: Two brow horns up to a meter long, a solid bony frill, and a parrot-like beak backed by hundreds of shearing teeth.
INFO_TRIKE_SPECULATIVE: The frill may have been brightly colored for showing off. Healed wounds suggest rivals locked horns, and it likely defended itself against T. rex.
INFO_TRIKE_FUN_FACT: Its first horns were mistaken for those of a giant bison.
INFO_ANKYLO_HABITAT: Forested lowlands of western North America.
INFO_ANKYLO_TRAITS: Covered in bony armor plates, even on its eyelids, with a heavy tail club that could break bones.
INFO_ANKYLO_SPECULATIVE: Probably earthy colors for camouflage. It may have dug up roots, and swung its club at predators and rivals.
INFO_ANKYLO_FUN_FACT: Looping air passages in its snout may have let it make deep, booming calls.
INFO_IGUANO_HABITAT: Wooded river valleys and swamps of Europe.
INFO_IGUANO_TRAITS: A sharp thumb spike, a grasping little finger, and teeth like a giant iguana's. It could walk on two legs or four.
INFO_IGUANO_SPECULATIVE: It probably lived in herds, kept in touch with honking calls, and used its thumb spike against predators.
INFO_IGUANO_FUN_FACT: The first models put its thumb spike on its nose, like a rhino horn.
INFO_SPINO_HABITAT: Rivers and tidal flats of North Africa.
INFO_SPINO_TRAITS: A tall sail on its back, a crocodile-like snout full of cone-shaped teeth, and a paddle-shaped tail.
INFO_SPINO_SPECULATIVE: Scientists still argue whether it swam after fish or waded like a giant heron. The sail may have been colorful for display.
INFO_SPINO_FUN_FACT: The first skeleton was destroyed by a bombing raid on Munich in 1944.
INFO_STEGO_HABITAT: Dry floodplains with conifers and ferns in western North America.
INFO_STEGO_TRAITS: Two rows of tall bony plates and four tail spikes. Its brain was only the size of a lemon.
INFO_STEGO_SPECULATIVE: The plates may have flushed with color to impress or warm up. A spike-shaped wound in an Allosaurus bone shows the tail was a real weapon.
INFO_STEGO_FUN_FACT: The spiked tail is called a "thagomizer", a name from a 1982 comic strip.
INFO_COMPY_HABITAT: Dry, scrubby islands in a warm, shallow sea in Europe.
INFO_COMPY_TRAITS: Turkey-sized, light and fast, with a long tail for balance. One fossil still has a lizard in its belly.
INFO_COMPY_SPECULATIVE: Probably covered in fuzzy feathers, maybe with a striped tail like its close relatives. It likely chased lizards and insects with quick darts.
INFO_COMPY_FUN_FACT: For over a century it was the smallest dinosaur known.
INFO_MOSASAURUS_HABITAT: Warm, shallow seas around the world.
INFO_MOSASAURUS_TRAITS: Flippers, a shark-like tail fin, and double-hinged jaws with an extra row of teeth on the roof of its mouth.
INFO_MOSASAURUS_SPECULATIVE: Dark on top and pale below, like a shark. It gave birth to live young at sea and likely ambushed prey from below.
INFO_MOSASAURUS_FUN_FACT: Its closest living relatives are monitor lizards and snakes.
INFO_UTAHRAPTOR_HABITAT: Dry floodplains with seasonal rivers in western North America.
INFO_UTAHRAPTOR_TRAITS: The biggest raptor known, with a curved sickle claw over 20 cm long on each foot.
INFO_UTAHRAPTOR_SPECULATIVE: Almost certainly feathered, like its relatives. It may have hunted in packs and pinned prey down with its claws.
INFO_UTAHRAPTOR_FUN_FACT: One block of sandstone holds several Utahraptors that may have been trapped in quicksand together.
INFO_PTERANODON_HABITAT: Coasts and open sea over the inland sea of North America.
INFO_PTERANODON_TRAITS: No teeth at all, a long crest on the back of its head, and hollow bones for soaring like an albatross.
INFO_PTERANODON_SPECULATIVE: Covered in fine hair-like fuzz, with a brightly colored crest. It probably skimmed or dived for fish and took off by vaulting on its wings.
INFO_PTERANODON_FUN_FACT: Over a thousand fossils have been found, more than of any other pterosaur.
GROUP_SYNAPSID: Synapsid: closer to mammals than to dinosaurs
INFO_PARASAURUS_HABITAT: Lush floodplains and forests of western North America.
INFO_PARASAURUS_TRAITS: A long hollow crest curving back from its head, with air tubes inside that ran from its nose.
INFO_PARASAURUS_SPECULATIVE: The crest worked like a trumpet, making deep, low calls that carried far. It may have been brightly colored for display.
INFO_PARASAURUS_FUN_FACT: Scientists rebuilt its skull on a computer and played its call: a low, rumbling horn.
INFO_NODOSAURUS_HABITAT: Coastal plains along an inland sea in North America.
INFO_NODOSAURUS_TRAITS: Bands of bony knobs across its back, but no tail club like Ankylosaurus.
INFO_NODOSAURUS_SPECULATIVE: It probably crouched low and let its armor take the bite. A close relative was found with reddish-brown skin and a pale belly.
INFO_NODOSAURUS_FUN_FACT: A relative from Canada is so well preserved it looks like a sleeping statue.
INFO_PROTO_HABITAT: Sand dunes and dry scrubland of Mongolia.
INFO_PROTO_TRAITS: Sheep-sized, with a parrot-like beak, a bony neck frill and no real horns.
INFO_PROTO_SPECULATIVE: It probably lived in groups and dug burrows or nests in the sand. The frill may have helped attract mates.
INFO_PROTO_FUN_FACT: One fossil was found locked in a fight with a Velociraptor.
INFO_PACHY_HABITAT: Forests and floodplains of western North America.
INFO_PACHY_TRAITS: A solid dome of bone on its head up to 25 cm thick, ringed with bony knobs.
INFO_PACHY_SPECULATIVE: Rivals may have shoved or butted each other with their domes. Its leaf-shaped teeth suggest it also ate fruit and seeds.
INFO_PACHY_FUN_FACT: Two smaller dinosaurs may turn out to be young Pachycephalosaurus with flatter heads.
INFO_DIPLO_HABITAT: Dry plains with rivers and conifer forests in western North America.
INFO_DIPLO_TRAITS: One of the longest animals ever to walk the earth, with a whip-like tail and peg-shaped teeth for stripping leaves.
INFO_DIPLO_SPECULATIVE: It may have cracked its tail like a whip to scare predators, and could perhaps rear up on its hind legs to reach high leaves.
INFO_DIPLO_FUN_FACT: Casts of one skeleton, nicknamed "Dippy", stand in museums all over the world.
INFO_TITANO_HABITAT: Warm plains and forests of India.
INFO_TITANO_TRAITS: A long-necked giant with bony armor plates set in its skin.
INFO_TITANO_SPECULATIVE: It probably laid its eggs in large nesting grounds, and the young had to grow up fast on their own.
INFO_TITANO_FUN_FACT: It gave its name to the titanosaurs, a group that includes the biggest land animals ever.
INFO_CERATO_HABITAT: Riverbanks and floodplains of western North America.
INFO_CERATO_TRAITS: A blade-like horn on its nose, bony bumps over the eyes and very long teeth for its size.
INFO_CERATO_SPECULATIVE: It may have hunted fish and crocodiles along rivers. The horn was probably for show, not for fighting.
INFO_CERATO_FUN_FACT: It had a row of small bony plates running down its back, unlike most carnivores.
INFO_RAPTOR_HABITAT: Deserts and sand dunes of Mongolia.
INFO_RAPTOR_TRAITS: Turkey-sized, with a curved killing claw on each foot and bumps on its arm bones where feathers grew.
INFO_RAPTOR_SPECULATIVE: Fully feathered, with winged arms. It probably hunted alone or in small groups, pinning prey with its claws.
INFO_RAPTOR_FUN_FACT: The raptors in movies are much bigger: the real one was about the size of a turkey.
INFO_GALLI_TRAITS: Long legs built for speed, a toothless beak, and big eyes on a small head.
INFO_GALLI_SPECULATIVE: It may have been one of the fastest dinosaurs. It was likely feathered and ate plants, insects and small animals.
INFO_GALLI_FUN_FACT: Its long neck and beak make it look like a giant ostrich.
INFO_HYPSI_HABITAT: Warm floodplains and forests of southern England.
INFO_HYPSI_TRAITS: Small and fast, with a beak at the front of its mouth and cheek teeth for chewing.
INFO_HYPSI_SPECULATIVE: It probably lived in herds and ran from danger. Some think it had a few simple feathers.
INFO_HYPSI_FUN_FACT: It was once wrongly thought to climb trees like a kangaroo in a forest.
INFO_ALCIONE_HABITAT: Coasts and shallow seas of North Africa.
INFO_ALCIONE_TRAITS: A small pterosaur with short, stout wing bones, living right at the end of the age of dinosaurs.
INFO_ALCIONE_SPECULATIVE: Its short wings may have helped it dive into the sea after fish, a bit like a kingfisher.
INFO_ALCIONE_FUN_FACT: It shows small pterosaurs were still around when the asteroid hit.
INFO_DEINOSUCHUS_HABITAT: Coastal swamps and river mouths of North America.
INFO_DEINOSUCHUS_TRAITS: One of the largest crocodile relatives ever, with teeth as big as bananas.
INFO_DEINOSUCHUS_SPECULATIVE: It probably ambushed dinosaurs at the water's edge. Bite marks on dinosaur bones fit its teeth.
INFO_DEINOSUCHUS_DISCOVERY: Black Creek Formation, North Carolina, USA (1858)
INFO_DEINOSUCHUS_FUN_FACT: It could grow for about 50 years, much longer than most dinosaurs.
INFO_DIMETRODON_HABITAT: Swampy river deltas of North America.
INFO_DIMETRODON_TRAITS: A tall sail on its back and two kinds of teeth: sharp stabbing ones and smaller shearing ones.
INFO_DIMETRODON_SPECULATIVE: The sail may have helped it warm up in the sun or show off to rivals.
INFO_DIMETRODON_FUN_FACT: It is not a dinosaur at all: it died out 40 million years before the first dinosaurs.
INFO_DUNKLEO_TRAITS: An armored head and self-sharpening bony blades instead of teeth.
INFO_DUNKLEO_SPECULATIVE: It could snap its jaws open fast enough to suck prey in, and had one of the strongest bites of any fish.
INFO_DUNKLEO_FUN_FACT: It lived over 100 million years before the first dinosaurs.
INFO_TORTOISE_TRAITS: One of the oldest turtles with a full shell. It could not pull its head inside.
INFO_TORTOISE_SPECULATIVE: Spikes on its neck and a clubbed tail probably protected it instead. It likely ate plants on land.
INFO_TORTOISE_FUN_FACT: Turtles were already around when the first dinosaurs appeared.
INFO_SALAMANDER_HABITAT: Lakes and ponds of Central Asia.
INFO_SALAMANDER_TRAITS: One of the oldest true salamanders, with a broad, rough skull.
INFO_SALAMANDER_SPECULATIVE: It probably lived on land as an adult and returned to water to breed, hunting insects and worms.
INFO_SALAMANDER_FUN_FACT: Salamanders have barely changed shape since the time of the dinosaurs.
INFO_DILOPHO_HABITAT: Rivers and floodplains of western North America.
INFO_DILOPHO_TRAITS: Two thin, rounded crests on its head and a notch in its upper jaw.
INFO_DILOPHO_SPECULATIVE: The crests were probably colorful for display. There is no evidence it spat venom or had a neck frill.
INFO_DILOPHO_FUN_FACT: It was the biggest land predator of its time.
INFO_RHAMPHO_HABITAT: Island lagoons of a warm, shallow sea in Europe.
INFO_RHAMPHO_TRAITS: Long, forward-pointing teeth and a long tail ending in a diamond-shaped vane.
INFO_RHAMPHO_SPECULATIVE: It likely skimmed fish from the water. The tail vane may have been brightly colored.
INFO_RHAMPHO_FUN_FACT: One fossil shows it being caught by a big fish while it held a fish of its own.
INFO_COELACANTH_MEANING: Named after the explorer and geologist Douglas Mawson
INFO_COELACANTH_HABITAT: Rivers, lakes and coastal seas of Africa and South America.
INFO_COELACANTH_TRAITS: A giant coelacanth with fleshy, limb-like fins and heavy scales.
INFO_COELACANTH_SPECULATIVE: It probably swallowed fish whole. Like living coelacanths, it may have lived very long and given birth to live young.
INFO_COELACANTH_FUN_FACT: Coelacanths were thought extinct until a living one was caught in 1938.
INFO_PSITTACO_HABITAT: Forests and lakes of East Asia.
INFO_PSITTACO_TRAITS: A parrot-like beak, bony cheek horns and long bristles sticking up from its tail.
INFO_PSITTACO_SPECULATIVE: Its skin was dark on top and pale below, which helped it hide in shady forests.
INFO_PSITTACO_FUN_FACT: We know its real colors from pigment preserved in one fossil.

RAPTOR_CHALLENGE_CATALOG_HINT: Hint: talk to the raptor in the forest to take it on!
LAVA_RACE_DESCRIPTION: Set a record for the lava obstacle course and win 10 coins!
TIP_DIET: Herbivores munch bushes and fruit, carnivores hunt, and everyone drinks at the water's edge.
TIP_EMPTY_METER: An empty food or water meter hurts you. Top them up before you head off exploring.
TIP_STAMINA: Running uses energy. Walk for a bit and it comes back.
TIP_STAND_STILL: Standing still refills your energy twice as fast as walking.
TIP_WATER_RUN: Running in water uses energy twice as fast as running on land.
TIP_FALL: A fall from high up hurts. Landing in deep water never does.
TIP_LAVA: Lava burns! Play the Velociraptor and hold forward and jump to leap across it.
TIP_EGG: Grown up? Keep eating, and an egg will appear in your starting nest.
TIP_COINS: Missions pay coins. Spend them on new looks for your dinosaur.
TIP_PRESTIGE: Prestige badges stay with you when you restart, and other players see them in multiplayer.
TIP_POKI_LOGIN: Log in on Poki to keep your progress and carry on from another device.
TIP_GRAPHICS: Game running slow? Lower the graphics settings in the pause menu.
TIP_JUMP_HIGH: Hold jump longer to jump higher.
TIP_KEYS: Shift to run, F to jump, Space to attack, E to eat, drink or use, R to roar.
TIP_SHORTCUTS: Shortcuts: L missions, J achievements, K map, Q power-ups, T customize, P photo mode, Esc settings.
TIP_EMOTES: In co-op, press T for emotes.
TIP_ROAR_STAMINA: A roar gives you back a little energy.
TIP_ROAR_BABIES: Roar and your cubs come running to you.
TIP_HIDE: Small dinos can hide in tall bushes. That includes you! Night hunters can't see you there...
TIP_TRUNKS: Smash fallen tree trunks. Some have nuts or mushrooms inside, and one hides much more.
TIP_SPEED_SHROOM: The speed mushroom costs you some food, but makes you fast for 30 seconds.
TIP_MUD: Roll in the mud pool for water protection. It lasts until you wash it off.
TIP_FOSSIL: Step up to a fossil to see your own skeleton.
TIP_SHARPEN: Rub against a sharpening rock for 30 seconds of stronger attacks.
TIP_MATING: Meet a grown dinosaur of your own kind for a mating dance and an instant egg.
TIP_SKIP_NIGHT: Night too scary? In the evening, the tab on the left skips you to daybreak.
TIP_PHOTO_KEYS: In photo mode: Shift zooms, T hides your own dinosaur, R roars for the shot.
TIP_DAY_CYCLE: You can turn off the day cycle and the weather in the settings.
TIP_BITE_PANIC: Bite a herbivore and the others of its kind nearby panic and run.
TIP_SMALL_HIDE: Small animals hide in bushes. Roar to scare them out.
TIP_ROAR_SCARE: A cub's roar scares almost no one. A big carnivore's roar makes everyone run.
TIP_TREX_ROAR: The Tyrannosaurus Rex doesn't flinch at anybody's roar.
TIP_ROAR_BACK: Roar near your own kind and they will roar back.
TIP_NIGHT_HUNTERS: At night, hunters attack anyone who comes close. Your own kind leaves you alone.
TIP_NIGHT_PLANT: At night, herbivores never hunt other herbivores.
TIP_RAPTOR_RIDE: Velociraptors leap onto bigger animals and ride them.
TIP_RAPTOR_SHAKE: A Velociraptor on your back? Run for three seconds, or hit back fast, to throw it off.
TIP_PTERANODON: Pteranodons fly off to drink at the lakes. Come too close and they circle away.
TIP_DRAGONFLY: Dragonflies like to land on you, but they fly off when it rains.
TIP_HOLLOW_TRUNK: Some hollow tree trunks have little dinosaurs hiding inside.
TIP_GIANTS: Diplodocus and Titanosaurus are so tall you can spot them from across the island.
TIP_BABY_EYES: Angry eyes on your screen at night mean something is after your cubs.
TIP_GALLI_RACE: Some Gallimimus will race you. Run past one to see if it's up for it.
TIP_EGG_HUNT: Find all 10 hidden eggs of a species to make it playable.
TIP_IGUANO: The Iguanodon is a fast runner.
TIP_LAVA_CHALLENGE: A Velociraptor in the forest has a lava challenge for you. Beat it to earn the Velociraptor.
TIP_BLACK_EGG: The black egg on the dinosaur picker is a secret. Look for red eyes in the dark…
TIP_AREAS: The Desert and the Forest open up at their gates for 400 coins.
TIP_MULTIPLAYER: Grow up fully and hatch an egg to unlock playing with real players.
TIP_CAMERA: Play a few minutes to unlock the camera, then snap animals for your Creature Catalog.
TIP_BADGES: Achievements earn prestige points, and prestige points earn badges.
TIP_EGG_SPOTS: Some eggs sit high up on ledges. Others hide behind bushes.
TIP_FEASTS: Giant feasts are hidden around the island. Can you find them all?
TIP_MUSHROOMS: Mushroom muncher: taste every mushroom on the island once.
TIP_FOSSILS_ROCKS: There are six fossils and six sharpening rocks to find.
TIP_BOULDERS: Boulders block some passages. Break them to open a shortcut.
TIP_LAVA_RECORD: Beat the lava course record and win 10 coins.
TIP_CROSS_RUN: The Cross-Continental Run takes you through every area of the island.
TIP_FIREFLIES: Fireflies come out over dry ground at night.
TIP_WEATHER: Sandstorms blow through the desert. Fog and rain roll in elsewhere.
TIP_PHOTO_GOALS: Photograph a sunset, a sunrise, a waterfall and a view from up high.
TIP_EVIL_COMPY: Some of the forest's Compsognathus aren't what they seem. Watch for red eyes at night.
TIP_LEADERBOARD: In multiplayer, the Daily Top Eaters board starts fresh every day.
TIP_COOP: Co-op: up to eight friends on your island. Send a link or a four-letter code.
TIP_GUIDING_ARROW: Lost? The Guiding Arrow points the way for a whole minute.
TIP_ARROW_EGGS: Stuck on an egg hunt? The Guiding Arrow knows where the last one is.
TIP_SPEED: With the Speed power-up, running costs no energy for 30 seconds.
TIP_ATTACK: Big fight coming? Attack doubles your bite for 30 seconds.
TIP_PROTECT: With Protect, every hit hurts half as much for 30 seconds.
TIP_THIRST: Long trek through the desert? Thirst Protection keeps you going.
TIP_HUNGER: Hunger Protection buys you time when food is far away.
TIP_NIGHT_VISION: Nights too dark? Night Vision lights them up for a minute.
TIP_EARN_COINS: Saving up for a skin? Earn Coins doubles your coins for two minutes.
TIP_SKY_RACE: A pteranodon in the desert runs the Sky Race. Fly through every ring in time to play as a pteranodon!
TIP_SKY_RACE_CANYON: A pteranodon on a high central cliff runs the Canyon Endurance Race. Land on the far nest to stop the clock.
TIP_FLY_DRAG: Drag the screen up and down to climb and dive more smoothly.
TIP_FLY_MOUSE: Fly more smoothly by turning on ‘Capture mouse cursor’ in Settings!
TIP_COOP_RACE: You can run races with your friends in Co-op mode! Which species will YOU bring to the challenge?
TIP_COOP_FLY: You can fly the air races in Co-op too! Try not to kill each other over the win...
TIP_FUN_FACTS: Snap photographs to get fun facts about all dinosaur species!
TIP_PARK_BABIES: Stand at your nest to leave your cubs there, then come back for them later.
RUN_CHOICE_TITLE: Pick up where you left off?
SKY_RACE_HINT: Win the Sky Race in the desert.
SKY_RACE_DETAILS: Roams the skies with this magnificent flying reptile!
SKY_RACE_DESCRIPTION:
Beat the race time and earn an exciting new playable creature!

Fly through every ring in 90 seconds. Three hearts, three attempts.
SKY_RACE_RECORD_DESCRIPTION: Beat the record and earn 10 coins!
SKY_RACE_CLIMB: Hold UP (F or Space) to take off and climb. The timer waits while you learn.
SKY_RACE_CLIMB_TOUCH: Hold {button} to take off and climb. The timer waits while you learn.
SKY_RACE_COLLECT: Return to the nest and collect the white egg!
SKY_RACE_RETRY: Time is up! Get ready for your next 90-second attempt.
SKY_RACE_TRY_AGAIN: Visit the guide to accept the challenge again.
SKY_RACE_CANYON_DESCRIPTION: Fly through the canyon and the bone tunnel, then land on the nest on the far cliff. Beat the record and earn 20 coins!
SKY_RACE_LAND: Land on the nest on the cliff!
WATER_RACE_DESCRIPTION: Swim from the waterfall around the rocks, dive through the underwater tunnel and run on into the canyon. Watch your air! Beat the record and earn 20 coins!
SALT_WATER_TEXT: Beware of salt water, this will make you sick and vomit
MAP_TAP_DOT: Tap a dot to see its name.
